hq_country: Belgium (Ramillies / Grand-Rosier; main R&D in Louvain-la-Neuve area)
target_vertical: Horizontal ERP; commonly deployed by manufacturers, multi-channel retailers, wholesalers/distributors, services firms
pricing_model: Per-user subscription with three tiers (One App Free, Standard, Custom); on-premise Community edition is free open-source. Connector apps (e.g. Amazon, Shopify) are bundled in Enterprise; some third-party connectors are paid In-App Purchases.
starting_price_usd: US Standard plan ~$24.90–$31.10 per user/month billed annually (promo-dependent); Custom/Enterprise ~$37.40–$46.70 per user/month. Community edition is free (self-hosted).
free_trial_or_freemium: 15-day free trial on Odoo Online; 'One App Free' plan (single app, unlimited users on Odoo Online); open-source Community edition is free forever.
shopify_supported: Native (Shopify connector module shipped with Odoo Enterprise) plus large third-party connector ecosystem on the Odoo Apps Store and Shopify App Store
shopify_app_listing_url: https://apps.shopify.com/odoo-integrator (third-party 'Odoo Integration ‑ Odoo ERP'); native module is delivered via Odoo, not the Shopify App Store
shopify_sync_direction: Bi-directional for products/inventory/customers/orders; orders typically pull from Shopify to Odoo, fulfilments/tracking push back to Shopify
shopify_synced_entities: Products, variants, collections/categories, images, inventory levels, customers, sales orders, fulfilments/shipments, refunds, payouts, taxes; recent native module additions include order/customer metafields and Shopify product webhooks (create/update/delete)
shopify_service_item_support: [uncertain] — Odoo supports service-type products natively; whether the native connector pushes them as Shopify services is not explicitly documented
shopify_multi_store_support: Yes — multiple Shopify stores can be connected to a single Odoo instance (native module and major third-party connectors)
shopify_pos_support: Indirect — Odoo has its own POS app; Shopify POS is not natively unified with Odoo POS. Shopify POS orders flow through the standard Shopify orders channel.
shopify_b2b_catalog_support: [uncertain] — no documented native support for Shopify Plus B2B company/location/price-list constructs; typically handled via Odoo pricelists and customer mapping
shopify_markets_support: [uncertain] — Shopify Markets (multi-market pricing, duties, landed cost) is not specifically called out in Odoo's native connector documentation
shopify_metafield_to_erp_field_mapping: Partial — recent native module additions support importing order and customer metafields into selectable Odoo fields; full generic metafield-to-custom-field mapping requires Odoo Studio or third-party connectors
shopify_variant_option_mapping: Variants map to Odoo product variants via product attributes/values; SKUs are the matching key; up to Shopify's 3 option / 100 variant limits
shopify_real_time_or_batch: Hybrid — real-time via Shopify webhooks for orders/products/inventory plus scheduled cron jobs for catch-up syncs (frequency configurable)
shopify_known_limitations: Community forum reports of bugs across competing connectors; metafield mapping limited compared to dedicated middleware; B2B (Plus) constructs not natively modelled; Shopify Markets pricing/duty handling not explicit; many production-grade deployments rely on paid third-party connectors (Emipro, Webkul, VentorTech, Teqstars) rather than the stock module.
etsy_native_or_third_party: Third-party via Odoo Apps Store connectors (e.g. Webkul Etsy Odoo Bridge) and iPaaS tools (SyncSpider, Onlizer, Codisto-style middleware)
etsy_listing_creation_vs_sync_only: Depends on connector — Webkul's Etsy Odoo Bridge supports creating and updating Etsy listings from Odoo as well as syncing existing ones
etsy_inventory_sync: Stock changes after Etsy orders reflect in Odoo in near real-time via the third-party connector; reverse stock push from Odoo to Etsy supported
etsy_order_import: Real-time / scheduled import depending on connector; orders managed from Odoo backend
etsy_synced_entities: Listings, variations, inventory levels, orders, customers, attributes (per Webkul Etsy Odoo Bridge); shipments/receipts handled via Odoo delivery flow
etsy_known_limitations: [uncertain] — no canonical vendor-published limitation list; Etsy quirks around personalization fields, digital products, and variation inventory typically need connector-specific handling
amazon_supported: Native — Odoo ships an Amazon Connector module (Enterprise) using SP-API; third-party paid connectors (Emipro amazon_ept, Webkul) also exist
amazon_marketplaces: US, Canada, Mexico, Brazil, UK, Germany, France, Spain, Italy, Netherlands, Poland, Sweden, Egypt, Saudi Arabia, UAE, Turkey, India, Singapore, Australia, Japan
amazon_seller_types: FBA and FBM (both via native connector). Vendor Central is [uncertain] — not part of the standard native module.
amazon_synced_entities: Sales orders (FBA & FBM), order line items, customer records (FBM with PII access), listings (offers/price/stock on existing listings), stock moves for FBA, settlement reports, refunds/reimbursements (extended via third-party Amazon Connector PRO modules)
amazon_listing_creation: Native connector primarily syncs existing listings (matches by SKU); listing creation/catalog publishing is limited — third-party connectors (e.g. Emipro) add richer create/update flows
amazon_repricing_support: [uncertain] — no native repricer; repricing typically handled by third-party tools
amazon_buy_shipping: [uncertain] — Amazon Buy Shipping label purchase is not a documented native Odoo capability
amazon_fba_inbound_workflow: [uncertain] — FBA outbound and stock moves are handled natively; FBA inbound shipment plan creation is not a highlighted native feature and is typically managed outside Odoo or via third-party connectors
amazon_sp_api_inbound_v2024_03_20: [uncertain] — Odoo migrated to SP-API; specific support for the Fulfillment Inbound v2024-03-20 API is not documented publicly
amazon_settlement_report_handling: Native connector imports Amazon settlement reports and creates corresponding sale orders, invoices, and reconciliation entries; third-party 'Amazon Connector PRO' modules add deeper settlement reconciliation and reimbursement handling
amazon_marketplace_facilitator_tax_handl: Marketplace-collected tax can be configured via Odoo tax mappings/fiscal positions; specific handling per marketplace facilitator rules is configuration-dependent
amazon_multi_account_support: Yes — multiple Amazon seller accounts can be connected to one Odoo instance
amazon_known_limitations: Native connector focuses on order/stock/settlement sync — listing creation, repricing, Buy Shipping, and FBA inbound workflows generally require third-party modules; complex multi-marketplace tax/fiscal position setup is non-trivial.
xero_supported: Third-party only — no native Xero module from Odoo S.A.
xero_app_store_certified: [uncertain] — Odoo is not listed as a certified app on the Xero App Store; integration is delivered via third-party Odoo connectors or generic iPaaS (Zapier, Make)
xero_synced_entities: Via third-party connectors: invoices (ACCREC), bills (ACCPAY), payments, contacts (customers/suppliers), products, accounts, payment terms, taxes, tracking categories; credit notes vary by connector
xero_accounting_sync_mode: invoice_per_order (per third-party connectors — each Odoo invoice/bill maps 1:1 to a Xero invoice/bill); summary-journal mode is not a typical Odoo→Xero pattern (Odoo itself runs full accounting)
xero_cogs_journal_method: [uncertain] — typically not relevant because Odoo runs its own perpetual or periodic inventory valuation and posts COGS internally; Xero usually only receives sales/purchase invoices, not full COGS journals
xero_multi_currency: Connector-dependent — major third-party Xero connectors support multi-currency invoice/bill posting where both systems are configured for multi-currency
xero_tracking_category_mapping: Some third-party connectors map Odoo analytic accounts/tags or fields to Xero tracking categories (connector-specific)
xero_tax_handling: Tax codes / tax rates mapped from Odoo taxes to Xero tax rates via the connector configuration; GST/VAT/sales-tax depends on regional setup
xero_known_limitations: No official Odoo-built or Xero-certified connector; reliance on third-party (and varying quality) connectors creates fragmentation; double-bookkeeping risk because Odoo is itself a full accounting platform — typical pattern is Odoo as system of record and Xero kept in sync only where required.
qb_online_supported: Third-party — multiple paid connectors on the Odoo Apps Store and via VentorTech, Webkul, Bista, etc. No native QBO module from Odoo S.A.
qb_desktop_supported: Third-party connectors exist for QuickBooks Desktop via web connector / file-based exchange; far less common than QBO connectors
qb_app_certified: [uncertain] — Odoo is not a featured Intuit App Store listing; connectors are sold and distributed through the Odoo Apps Store
qb_synced_entities: Invoices, bills, payments, customers, vendors, products/items, taxes, accounts, payment terms/methods, departments (connector-specific); inventory adjustments and COGS journals are generally NOT pushed because Odoo keeps inventory accounting internally
qb_accounting_sync_mode: invoice_per_order (typical) — each Odoo invoice/bill mirrors to QBO; some connectors offer scheduled batch or real-time modes and bi-directional sync
qb_cogs_journal_method: [uncertain] — Odoo manages COGS internally (perpetual via automated valuation in AVCO/FIFO or periodic via Standard costing); only invoices typically flow to QBO
qb_multi_currency: Supported by major third-party connectors when both Odoo and QBO are configured for multi-currency
qb_class_location_mapping: [uncertain] — depends on the connector; not a standardized feature
qb_known_limitations: Fragmented connector market with variable quality; overlapping functionality with Odoo Accounting can cause reconciliation issues; most deployments either use Odoo Accounting natively or use QBO only as a secondary reporting/tax system.
other_ecom_channels: WooCommerce (native module + many third-party connectors), eBay (native module via Enterprise + third-party), Magento/Adobe Commerce (third-party), BigCommerce (third-party), Walmart (third-party), TikTok Shop (third-party), Wix/Squarespace (third-party), Faire (third-party), Square (third-party), PrestaShop (third-party); Odoo's own eCommerce app is also a first-party storefront option
bundle_kit_component_decomposition: Supported via Kit BOMs (BoM type = Kit) — selling a kit decrements component stock; also supported in Manufacturing via standard multi-level BOMs
bom_support: Yes — core to the Manufacturing (MRP) app
multi_level_bom: Yes — unlimited BOM levels, Odoo auto-explodes sub-assemblies and creates separate manufacturing orders for intermediate items as required
production_orders: Yes — Manufacturing Orders, Work Orders, Routings/Operations, Work Centers, capacity planning, shop floor app (Enterprise), quality checkpoints, maintenance integration
batch_lot_tracking: Yes — lot tracking with expiry dates, FEFO removal strategy, GS1 barcode support for lots
serial_tracking: Yes — full serial-number tracking with forward/backward traceability and GS1 barcode support
bin_location_support: Yes — multi-level storage locations (warehouse > location > sub-location/bin) with per-location barcodes
multi_warehouse: Yes — multiple warehouses, inter-warehouse transfers, push/pull rules per route
barcoding: Yes — built-in Barcode app, label generation, GS1/EAN13/EAN14/Code128/QR support; mobile barcode flows via the Odoo mobile app and third-party scanner apps
purchase_orders: Yes — RFQs, PO confirmation, partial receipts, vendor pricelists, multi-vendor matrix, blanket orders (Enterprise), Suggest quantities (history-based reorder)
supplier_management: Yes — vendor records, lead times, MOQs, supplier-specific pricelists, supplier-SKU mapping per product, supplier evaluation
landed_cost_support: Yes — Landed Costs feature allocates freight, duties, insurance, etc. to inventory cost. Requires AVCO or FIFO costing with automated inventory valuation; not available with Standard costing.
multi_currency_inventory_valuation: Single base currency for valuation per company (multi-company supports per-company currencies); purchase cost can be in foreign currency with FX revaluation
ai_demand_forecasting: Yes — Odoo 19 (2025) introduced native AI-driven demand forecasting that learns from sales history and seasonality and feeds reorder rules; third-party AI add-ons (AI Demand Sense, Datup, GMDH) also available
ai_purchase_order_suggestions: Yes — Odoo 19 auto-generates Purchase Orders or Manufacturing Orders when AI-predicted stock falls below thresholds; older 'Suggest quantities' feature uses historical demand averages
ai_natural_language_query: Yes — Odoo 19 ships an integrated AI assistant capable of natural-language interactions across the suite; depth of 'ask your inventory' style queries is evolving
public_api: Yes — public External API exposed via XML-RPC and JSON-RPC (legacy) and a new External JSON-2 API in Odoo 19; community/third-party REST wrappers exist; access to all public ORM model methods
webhook_event_coverage: Outbound webhooks configured via Odoo Studio + Base Automation on any model event (create/update/delete/state changes); inbound triggers via API endpoints. Coverage is configurable rather than a fixed event catalog.
integration_architecture: Native first-party connectors for major channels (Shopify, Amazon, eBay, WooCommerce) plus a large iPaaS-style marketplace of third-party connectors on the Odoo Apps Store; also Zapier/Make/n8n; on-prem extensibility via Python modules and Studio
zapier_make_support: Yes — official Zapier app and Make/n8n connectors available
mobile_app: Yes — official Odoo mobile apps for iOS and Android wrap the responsive web UI; Field Service, Inventory, POS and Barcode flows are usable on mobile
mobile_barcode_scanning_app: Yes — built-in Barcode app is mobile-friendly (Chrome/Safari); dedicated third-party native apps (e.g. Ventor) provide deeper Android/iOS barcode UX
rate_limit_handling_documented: Partial — Shopify GraphQL/REST rate limiting, retry, and error handling are documented in third-party connectors (e.g. integration_shopify PRO); native connector documentation acknowledges throttling for Amazon SP-API. Comprehensive public rate-limit handling docs across all channels are not centralized.
sync_frequency: Shopify: real-time via webhooks + cron (configurable, often 5-15 min). Amazon: scheduled SP-API polling (typically hourly + on-demand). Xero/QBO via third-party: real-time on post or scheduled. WooCommerce: webhooks + cron.
shipping_carrier_integrations: Native connectors for FedEx, UPS, USPS, DHL Express, Canada Post, bpost, EasyPost, Sendcloud, Shiprocket, Australia Post, Mondial Relay; extension modules add DPD, GLS, Hermes, PostNL, Aramex, Royal Mail, Deutsche Post, Shippo, Parcel.eu, Aftership, ShipStation, EasyShip and more
shipping_label_buying: Yes — in-app label purchase via integrated carrier modules (rates calculated on sale order, labels and tracking numbers generated from the delivery order)
three_pl_integrations: Third-party connectors available for ShipBob, ShipHero, ShipMonk, 3PL Central / Extensiv; EDI / API integration patterns are common
edi_support: Yes — Odoo supports EDI for invoicing in regulated markets (e.g. Peppol, Factur-X, ZUGFeRD, regional e-invoicing); broader retail/wholesale EDI (X12/EDIFACT 850/855/856/810) requires third-party modules or middleware
g2_rating: ~4.3/5 across ~1,200+ reviews on G2 (Odoo ERP product page)
g2_grid_quadrant: [uncertain] — Odoo appears in multiple G2 Grid reports across ERP/Inventory/Accounting; exact quadrant placement varies by category and quarter
other_accounting_integrations: Sage 50, Sage Intacct, Zoho Books, MYOB, FreshBooks, NetSuite — all via third-party connectors on the Odoo Apps Store or iPaaS (Zapier/Make/n8n). No native first-party module from Odoo S.A. for these systems. Odoo's own Accounting app is the default and is fully featured, so most deployments use Odoo Accounting natively rather than syncing to an external ledger.
notable_customers: Toyota Material Handling, Hyundai, Veolia, Danone (via subsidiaries), WWF, Toyota HQ Belgium, Singer, World Vision and ~12 million users / 5,000+ implementation partners worldwide (per Odoo)
last_major_release: Odoo 19 released October 2025 — headline additions include the native AI demand forecasting/auto-replenishment, integrated AI assistant across apps, the new External JSON-2 API, and shop floor / manufacturing enhancements
owner_parent_company: Odoo S.A. — privately held; major investors include Sequoia Capital, CapitalG (Alphabet), Summit Partners, Alkeon, AVP, BlackRock, HarbourVest, Mubadala
last_funding_event: November 2024 — €500M (≈$527M) secondary share sale led by CapitalG and Sequoia, valuing Odoo at ~€5B / $5.26B
public_status_page_uptime: https://status.odoo.com (Odoo Online status page); recent uptime figures not extracted in this pass [uncertain]
